observation.visible_scene: A high-speed-style shot against a pure black background. A vertical column of small, bright liquid droplets (a spray/stream) occupies the center-left of the frame throughout. At the bottom edge sit two rounded green objects with textured skin (lime/avocado-like): one at the bottom-left corner, one at the bottom-right.
visible_changes: The droplet column is present in every frame, but its internal pattern of individual droplets continuously rearranges frame to frame, indicating ongoing motion of the spray rather than a static pattern.
Relative to the frame, the droplet column drifts upward over the sequence (a bright leading droplet near the top climbs higher in successive frames), while the green objects drift downward.
The left green object progressively sinks out of the bottom edge and is gone by the later frames.
The right green object shifts from the bottom-right toward the bottom-center and stays partially visible at the bottom edge to the end.
The horizontal position and width of the droplet column stay broadly similar; the dominant change is vertical translation and internal reshuffling of droplets.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause or origin of the droplet spray (no onset or impact is shown).
Whether the vertical shift is actual object/droplet motion or a camera tilt/pan, since the black background offers no fixed reference.
What happens before the first frame and after the last; both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries.
The exact material of the green objects and the liquid.
uncertain_details: Direction of droplet motion (rising vs falling) cannot be separated from possible camera movement on the featureless black background.
Whether the column narrows or merely translates is not clearly resolvable.
The two green objects' motion relative to each other is small and may be partly camera-induced.
